findings.title: Ordinary non-POSIX constructor still imports fcntl
causal_path: The main and bind_cli_provider guards avoid entrypoint/native imports on non-POSIX.
An ordinary unbound HermesCLI constructor continues past bind_cli_provider and unconditionally imports friday_cli_output to initialize console output.
friday_cli_output imports fcntl at module top level and imports friday_cli_fd, which also imports fcntl at top level.
On a non-POSIX platform without fcntl, ordinary chat construction still fails before normal model/runtime startup even with no Friday/native binding.
findings.required_change: Preserve ordinary non-POSIX construction by gating or deferring the POSIX-only output/descriptor implementation at the actual constructor boundary; keep unsupported native Friday result refused. Review the complete retained constructor/import path, not only main/bind_cli_provider.

findings.title: Public PluginState.set still changes pinned serializer/error behavior
causal_path: Original public set normalizes json.dumps TypeError/ValueError into ValueError for a non-JSON-serializable value.
Current public set performs json.dumps directly outside that normalization.
A bytes/object/set or other nonserializable value now escapes as TypeError instead of the original ValueError; default nonfinite value handling also changed globally through allow_nan=False.

Removing the native get/set redirect restores directory/lock compatibility but does not restore this retained public input/error contract. This affects ordinary plugin calls independently of native authority.
findings.required_change: Restore the pinned public serializer/error compatibility or supply an explicit deliberate API change and its consumer obligations; keep stronger native set_commit serializer/private custody rules separate. At minimum retain the public ValueError normalization for invalid JSON values.

findings.trigger: An exact future accepted standard Thread.start/direct original frontend creator site is reached with Source actors plus retained native threads already at resources.owned_threads (the schema permits 4, consumed by two fixture readers, reaper and controller).

The global trace wrapper catches that BaseException, records only observer_error and bus.stop, then returns its trace callback.

The original Thread.start call proceeds to kernel acquisition because its trace call returned normally. The Source owns no retained generation for this attempted actor and its four-thread declaration did not stop the fifth acquisition.

Thread enumeration and guardian-required UNKNOWN later cannot turn that Source before-effect check into a performed refusal or recover a quick exited birth. Source actor registration itself is improved; this native frontend branch remains different.

Keep observation errors distinct from an effect guard, retain attempted generation/partial-start facts, and preserve all foreign/late actors as UNKNOWN. findings.title: Shared cli_bound wrapper code is mistaken for the original frontend function
findings.trigger: The correctly qualified original HermesCLI constructor invokes its ordinary @cli_bound _init_session_store before NativeProducer invokes the actual @cli_bound HermesCLI.run.
causal_path: The pinned cli_bound factory returns bound(self,*args,**kwargs); every decorated method has a distinct function/closure but the same bound.__code__. HermesCLI.run and CLIInitMixin._init_session_store both use that factory.

NativeRuntime forces the frontend_run callable to be the actual cli class run attribute. Its code is consequently the shared wrapper code; exact hash/filename/qualname qualification does not identify which decorated function owns a particular frame.

Observer.trace tests frame.f_code against frontend_run.__code__ with no expected function/closure/callee predicate. During CLI construction it records _init_session_store as native_frontend_frame, starts the case clock and then records its return as native_frontend_returned.

The controller, started after construction, immediately observes that alleged native return and leaves before driving the real input plan. Evidence also assigns a wrong frontend clock/return; the later intact actual run can remain undriven.

The required native frontend creator body is decorated too. resolve_attribute denies __wrapped__ and nested_code traverses only co_consts, so a site row using the raw HermesCLI.run qualname cannot find that creator body through the currently accepted run attribute; a wrapper site cannot match the raw creator line. Supplying a fresh map alone does not resolve this original decorated-function boundary.
findings.required_change: Retain and qualify the exact original decorator target/closure/function ownership and correlate trace frames to that callable. Bind frontend entry/return and direct creator sites to the actual run body or an exact original wrapper predicate; distinguish constructor and unrelated decorated calls. Do not bypass cli_activity, create an alias product entrypoint or transfer old Safety. Recheck constructor startup, genuine frontend dispatch, original outer input and same-code foreign/unrelated wrapper calls together.
